column1: # The index examples/typst-numbering.qmd prints in a Typst render (M099).
# Derived BY HAND from that source, under the ORACLE RULE at the head of
# tests/run-tests.sh, and never copied from a render. The row shape is the one
# tests/typst-index-main.tsv states. A locator of several words is written
# with the single spaces pdftotext puts between its words: `1 / 5`.
# Physical pages, from the source's page breaks and `set page` rules, with the
# page counter on each and the pattern in force:
#   page 1  counter 1                  `1 / 1`
#   page 2  counter 2                  `1 / 1`
#   page 3  counter 1 (reset to 1)     `1 / 1`
#   page 4  counter 2                  `1 / 1`
#   page 5  counter 2 (reset to 2)     `i of I`
#   page 6  counter 3                  `- 1 -`
#   page 7  counter 4                  none
#   page 8  counter 5, the index       `1 / 1`
# The index holds twelve one-line entries under twelve letter groups, which fit on
# one page, so page 8 is the last page. The final value of the page counter is
# therefore 5: 2 on page 5, plus one for each of pages 6, 7 and 8. A pattern
# naming two counters prints it as `5`, or as `V` for `I`.
# So a locator prints `1 / 5` on pages 1 and 3, `2 / 5` on pages 2 and 4,
# `ii of V` on page 5, `- 3 -` on page 6, and the physical page `7` on page 7.
# Under M100 a locator's class and value order the locators, and a range spans
# the values from its opening value to a greater closing value of one class.
# Pages 1 to 4 and 6 are arabic, `1 / 1` and `- 1 -` both naming `1` first,
# with the counter as the value. Page 5 is lower roman, value 2. Page 7, with
# no numbering, is arabic with its physical page, 7, as the value. The rows
# for birch, fern, holly and lime were rederived under these rules in M100.
#   apple    pages 1 and 3 print one text: one locator, linked to page 1
#   birch    a range from page 1 to page 3, both ends `1 / 5`: a single mark,
#            value 1, that spans nothing; the mark on page 2, value 2, prints
#   cedar    ordinary on page 1, principal on page 3, one text: one bold
#            locator, linked to page 1
#   dune     ranges 1-2 and 3-4, both `1 / 5–2 / 5`: one locator, linked to 1
#   elm      a range opened and closed on page 1 and a mark on page 3, one
#            text: one locator, linked to page 1
#   fern     a range from page 2 to page 3, closing on a lower value, spans
#            nothing; a mark on page 2, the range's opening page, prints, and
#            before the range, as a single mark closes on an earlier page
#   gorse    one mark under `i of I`, page 5
#   holly    page 4 (arabic 2) and page 5 (lower roman 2) print two texts: two
#            locators, lower roman first
#   iris     one mark under `- 1 -`, page 6
#   juniper  one mark on page 7, which has no numbering
#   kale     pages 1, 2 and 3: `1 / 5` once, where page 1 puts it, then `2 / 5`
#   lime     a range from page 1 to page 2 spans values 1 and 2; the marks on
#            page 2 and page 4 both have value 2 and print nothing
